ops.title: Agent edits in the main jj checkout get silently swept into the user's mid-session `jj squash` and can ship unreviewed — isolate impl agents or gate on op log
ops.body:
2026-07-09: an implementation agent edited in the main cc-pool checkout while the user was finishing their own change there. jj snapshotted the agent's edits into the shared working-copy change; the user's `jj squash -m "fix(daemon,cli): …TCC…"` folded them into the TCC commit, and within minutes the user pushed main and tagged a release — the agent's credential-parsing code shipped publicly BEFORE its review pass, under a commit message that never mentioned it. The agent ran zero mutation commands; the collision is structural (shared working copy + user committing mid-session).

**Why:** jj auto-absorbs every working-tree edit into `@`; two writers in one checkout means one squash/commit owns both. This user commits and cuts releases mid-session, in parallel sessions (see [[reverify-commits-before-extracting]], [[ok-to-cut-releases-unprompted]]).

**How to apply:** Run implementation agents with worktree isolation (`isolation: "worktree"` / EnterWorktree) whenever the user may touch the repo concurrently — mind [[jj-branch-delete-abandons-unpushed-ancestry]] on cleanup. If an agent must edit the main checkout, record `jj op log` position before dispatch and diff it after; review the isolated agent diff via evolog predecessors (`git diff <pre-squash-commit> <last-snapshot>`) if absorbed. Same incident: a release was cut anchored on the INSTALLED version (v0.49.1 after v0.50.0 existed) — semver-backward tag regressed the Homebrew tap; remediation = roll forward (delete bad release+tag, re-tag higher on the same or newer commit) and rewrite the new release's notes manually, since deleting the previous tag breaks the auto-notes compare range.
